The very narrow 90% confidence interval for tomorrow, from 580.0 to 604.0, suggests that short-term movements are typically quite constrained and predictable. However, as we look out to one week, the interval expands significantly (565.0 to 620.0), acknowledging that a greater range of outcomes becomes possible as daily fluctuations accumulate and new information has more time to emerge. Several specific risks or events could push outcomes beyond these stated intervals. Conversely, major economic downturns, unforeseen geopolitical crises, a severe negative earnings report (if this pertains to a company stock), or a broad market correction could cause a precipitous drop, pushing the value well below the lower bounds. These types of high-impact, low-probability events represent the "tail risks" that could dramatically alter the forecasted trajectory.
